head: 6e0e41af73ed8a7f8772f0251836a69c55406df4

subject: task-notifications
reasons: Cursor is marked absent, but its changelog documents the behaviour in part. It says "Background task follow-ups are back. Completion follow-ups for finished background tasks fire again in interactive and headless sessions", and "Background subagents include their final message in the completion notification". These lines document owner notification when a background task finishes, which is the statement's 'otherwise as a new turn' half. The changelog also does not document the whole area, so silence about delivery inside a running turn does not show that Cursor lacks the capability. Cursor needs a supported or pending cell, or a narrower statement.

That is waking the agent after a delay with a prompt. The page only lacks the clamping and the time acknowledgment, so it is silent on those parts rather than saying they are unsupported. It also covers scheduling, not a full list of options, so silence does not show absence. The absent claim is not supported.

reasons: claude-mock/internal/runner/control_fork.go:10-17 and 28-31 (claudeForkSchema IsBoundary/IsSummary and preservedUUIDs) interpret the compact_boundary subtype, isCompactSummary flag and compactMetadata.preservedMessages.uuids, which is what the compaction sequence preserves and duplicates the boundary reading in control_boundary.go; move them into internal/compaction (or the compaction home files) and have the fork code call that API. Checklist: event.go:31 and :32 (PreCompact/PostCompact constants) are uses; control_fork.go:11, :14 and :29 are leaks; record.go:21 is a comment on a decoded field, a use.

subject: posttooluse-payload
reasons: The stops run shows three PreToolUse hooks (echo DENYME, EXIT2ME, FINE) but only one PostToolUse (echo FINE), so a call refused by PreToolUse gets no PostToolUse. No test marked sr:proves posttooluse-payload/codex asserts this. TestOneDenyAmongHooksRefusesAndAskDoesNot and TestRefusedCallDoesNotRunAndTheTurnGoesOn belong to pretooluse-refusal, and the second registers PostToolUse without asserting that it did not fire. Everything else in the checklist is covered: tool_name, tool_input, tool_response, turn_id, tool_use_id, firing after a non-zero exit, and no duration_ms.
head: 5182187b8f2d86c0ce50b3fdc0868dc045d7976f

subject: hook-output-transcript-records
reasons: The docs say PreToolUse and PostToolUse `additionalContext` is added as developer context, and that PostToolUse `continue: false` replaces the tool result with the hook's feedback. No sr:proves test for hook-output-transcript-records/codex covers any of the three. The PostToolUse `additionalContext` case appears only in capabilities_test.go, under hook-additional-context. `Interpret` and `readOutput` in decide.go do not handle `continue: false` for PostToolUse at all. The recorded runs and the other checklist items I traced are covered: silent success, exit 1 and timeout leaving no record, tool-call blocks as the call's result, stop blocks as hook_prompt, and a blocked prompt leaving no record.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: noninteractive-run
reasons: The docs state that piped stdin is added as context to a prompt argument and that `codex exec -` reads the whole prompt from stdin (the 'Advanced stdin piping' section), but the mock never reads stdin (exec.go joins args only), no deviation declares this, and no test covers it. Also, every recorded stream (stops, hook-exit-codes, prompt-blocked) has two item.completed events with subtype error right after thread.started, and stops/hook-exit-codes have several intermediate agent_message items, yet TestNonInteractiveRunStreamsEventsAndEndsOnce pins the exact shape thread.started, turn.started, command_execution, turn.completed with none of these.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: session-end-hook
reasons: The doc (hooks#sessionend) says the SessionEnd hook can still read the session transcript while it runs, but no test has a SessionEnd hook read the file transcript_path names (transcript_file_test only probes the start and stop hooks); the doc also lists archive/delete and 30-minute-idle triggers, which no test covers and no codex deviation declares.
head: a4c123f61390efe395773e0882b17e14e3dbf283

subject: session-end-hook
reasons: The existing tests match the recorded run (SessionEnd fires last with reason other, no model or permission_mode, hook output unrecorded, synchronous even when async, failures do not end the run abnormally). But the codex doc (hooks#sessionend) also says SessionEnd fires on archive/delete of an open conversation and after 30 minutes idle, and never runs for subagents. The mock models none of these, no test covers them, and session-end-hook.yaml declares no codex deviation for them. Add a codex modeled-surface deviation for these cases, or add tests and recordings.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: stop-block-continuation
reasons: The Codex Stop doc says that when several matching Stop hooks run, `continue: false` from any one takes precedence over another hook's block/continuation decision. No test covers this and no deviation declares it: the mock's EndOfTurn (turn_host.go) returns on the first blocking hook and ignores `continue: false`. TestStopBlockContinuesTheTurnWithOneEnd also only checks that the reason text appears somewhere in the rollout. It does not check that the reason was handed back as a new user prompt, which the doc describes.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: stop-hook-payload
reasons: TestStopPayloadCarriesLastMessageAndContinuing only checks last_assistant_message == "DONE" and stop_hook_active false then true across two Stops; the doc's `last_assistant_message: string | null` (null when no assistant message is available) variant is never exercised, and the recorded third Stop (still stop_hook_active:true after a second block, per the stops sample) is not asserted by this capability's test.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: stop-hook-payload
reasons: Codex is marked supported with no deviations, but the statement claims the Stop payload carries the background tasks still running. The Codex doc's Stop table lists only turn_id, stop_hook_active and last_assistant_message. The Stop payloads in codex-mock/snapshots/runs/stops contain no background-tasks field. Add that part as a Codex deviation, or drop it from the statement.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: user-prompt-submit-hook
reasons: The codex test (TestUserPromptSubmitAddsContextOrRefuses) leaves several documented behaviours untested. (1) The refusal case only checks the stream shape [thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed] from a replay of the prompt-blocked recording. It never asserts that the agent did not run `echo SHOULDNOTRUN`, that no tool or PreToolUse event occurred, that stderr carried PROMPT-BLOCK-MSG, or that the prompt payload was logged. (2) The docs also describe blocking with JSON {"decision":"block","reason":...} and adding context with JSON hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. Neither is exercised, only plain stdout and exit 2. (3) The statement says the hook fires for a background-task notification handed to the agent. No test covers it, and there is no codex deviation declaring it unmodeled. (4) The hook-exit-codes run shows UserPromptSubmit with SessionStart exit 2 and exit 0 on stdout. The test checks only the BANANA context path in the mock, not that exit-0 plain stdout leaves the turn running while other hooks fire.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: user-prompt-submit-hook
reasons: Codex is cited as fully supported with no deviations, but neither its doc (#userpromptsubmit, which only covers additionalContext and block/exit 2) nor its runs (hook-exit-codes, prompt-blocked) show the hook firing for a background-task notification or that a hook cannot rewrite the prompt; those parts must be grounded by a run or listed as deviations.
head: 218d21b2a58c3f470f719e6b7c2aff2c5116e790

subject: noninteractive-run
reasons: Every recorded codex run (stops, hook-exit-codes, prompt-blocked) streams two item.completed events of item type error between thread.started and turn.started, but streamShape in replay_test.go:149 filters error items out and no noninteractive-run test asserts or even mentions them. The prompt-blocked run (thread.started, errors, turn.started, then turn.completed with no items, because the prompt was refused) is never driven by a test marked sr:proves noninteractive-run/codex. The 'ends with one result' check also never covers a run with zero agent_message or command items.
head: 268f1150594fc12ea5a5edd2f2866d43a8aa0e76

subject: subagent-stop-block-loop
reasons: The two tests (subagent_stop_test.go) check only hook_event_name and stop_hook_active for the six payloads, so the recorded agent_id, agent_type "default", session_id and permission_mode on SubagentStart/SubagentStop are never asserted; the doc's SubagentStop fields turn_id and last_assistant_message and its "matcher is applied to agent_type" variant (match vs non-match skipping the block loop) have no test and no deviation; and no test pins the feedback hook_prompt wrapper.
head: 268f1150594fc12ea5a5edd2f2866d43a8aa0e76

You are a sub-agent: you cannot get the user's words yourself (your prompt is your parent's, not the user's), and you cannot ask the user. Do not leave this for the parent to cover at merge with a trailer — that grounds nothing. Hand the change back instead:
1. Save it as a patch file outside the repository (a file, never a branch, tag or stash: any ref holding it is judged at your Stop too):
  `git diff --binary bf1f4613722944beb8ad35ddd60ff417a839e9a3..HEAD -- adr/mock-compaction-trigger/ADR.md > "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/handback.patch"`
2. Revert those files on your branch in a real commit, so your branch carries nothing uncited:
  `git apply -R --index "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/handback.patch" && git commit -m 'revert: handed back to the parent for the user approval'`
3. Report to your parent: where the patch is ("${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/handback.patch"), and EXACTLY what needs the user's approval. The parent asks the user (AskUserQuestion), re-applies the patch (`git apply --index <patch>`), and commits it with `Sloprail-Cites-User: <the user's exact answer>`.
